facts.value: Total borrowing £197.6m at 31.3.2026 (down £4.6m from £202.3m at 31.3.2025), weighted rate 3.77%, weighted average maturity 12.3 years. PWLB £158.7m at 3.7% (15.2 yrs); Welsh Gov interest-free £5.9m at 0.0% (2.4 yrs); LA/Other £33.0m at 4.7% (0.1 yrs); Banks/LOBO £0.0m.

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Table 3, appendix §3.6, page 5-6 (identical table also at covering §5, page 3). PWLB rose £13.2m as short-term LA borrowing fell £17.0m — the switch is documented in Table 4 (£23m of new long-dated PWLB) and confirmed by the Table 9 budget variance (+£644k on PWLB interest, −£690k on short-term interest).

facts.value: General Fund CFR £226.8m at 31.3.2026 (up £17.2m from £209.6m at 31.3.2025). Loans CFR (General Fund CFR less Other debt liabilities of £1.8m) £225.0m. Forecast: £237.1m (31.3.2027), £237.5m (31.3.2028), £237.7m (31.3.2029).

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Table 1 (appendix §2.1, page 3) for actuals and quarterly path; Table 10 (appendix §8.2, page 13) for forward forecast. CFR growth of £17.2m in 2025/26 matches the £23m of new long-dated PWLB borrowing (Table 4) less amortisation of Welsh Gov (£0.8m), LA repayment (£17.0m) and MRP. Loans CFR flattens after 2027 (£237.5m to £237.7m over two years).

facts.value: £27.5m at 31.3.2026, up from £5.4m at 31.3.2025 — a £22.1m increase in the year.

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Table 1 'Net External borrowing' line, appendix §2.1, page 3. Paragraph 2.2 confirms: 'at the end of the financial year the Authority was internally borrowed by £27.5m, meaning that reserves and working capital were being used first, prior to taking external borrowing.' Balance sheet identity ties: 226.8 − 197.6 − 1.8 = 27.4 (£0.1m rounding on the intermediate Borrowing CFR line of £225.0m). Prior year ties to the pound: 209.6 − 202.3 − 1.9 = 5.4. Internal borrowing is 12% of Loans CFR at 31.3.2026 — modest by our library.

facts.value: £17.7m at 31.3.2026 (£16.0m at 31.3.2025), average income return 4.33% (5.17% in 24/25). Mix: MMFs £8.7m, cash equiv £10.7m (net £3.0m gov/LA), unsecured banks/BS £2.0m, pooled funds £4.0m. Range during the year £11.0m-£48.0m.

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Table 6, appendix §4.2, page 8. Investment weighted average maturity is 20 days per Table 7 benchmarking (§4.6) — well below Similar LAs cohort at 105 days but roughly twice the All-LAs mean at 10 days. Bail-in exposure 78% vs 40% for Similar LAs, structural feature of a small (£17.7m) book with £4m pooled funds and £8.7m MMFs. Pooled funds returned 5.39% income plus £209k unrealised capital gain; cumulative unrealised losses stand at £178k, backed by a £590k treasury risk reserve (§4.9, §4.11).

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Table 10, appendix §8.2, page 13-14. Paragraph 8.3: 'if capital plans remain accurate, the Council will have a borrowing requirement over the medium term of £93.1m.' The £77.1m falling inside 12 months is composed almost entirely of the £70.1m fall in the current loan profile — the £33m LA/Other short-term book (0.1 yrs weighted, Table 3) rolling off plus circa £26m of PWLB and Welsh Gov short-dated maturities, plus £7m of rising benchmark. Balance sheet resources plateau at £42.5m from 2027 onward. Liquidity allowance of £10m turns on from 31.3.2027.

facts.value: 30% of total borrowing (£59.28m of £197.6m) matures within 12 months at 31.3.2026 (was 31% at 31.3.2025). 12-24 months bucket 8% (£15.81m). Combined inside two years: 38% or £75.09m.

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Table 12, appendix §8.8, page 15. All buckets within limits (upper 50% for under-12m; 30% for the rest). Composition of the under-12m bucket: £33m LA/Other short-term (Table 3, weighted 0.1 yrs), plus £5.9m Welsh Gov (2.4 yrs — likely 12-24m bucket, not under-12m), plus circa £20m of PWLB short-dated maturities. Our file shows 5 PWLB loans totalling £9.09m under 12 months at weighted 4.686% — the remainder of the PWLB short-dated exposure is at 1-2 years (£3.49m at 6.047%) and 2-5 years (£15.80m at 3.381%).

facts.value: £23.0m of new long-dated PWLB borrowing during 2025/26 across five loans at 4.51%-4.85%: EIP 14/04 £3.0m at 4.51% for 5.0 yrs; EIP 14/10 £5.0m at 4.85% for 9.5 yrs; EIP 22/10 £3.0m at 4.67% for 10.0 yrs; EIP 14/01 £5.0m at 4.67% for 9.0 yrs; Maturity 10/03 £7.0m at 4.59% for 1.17 yrs.

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Table 4, appendix §3.8, page 7. Four EIP tranches (amortising) plus one 14-month Maturity loan replacing a short-dated maturity. Weighted rate across the £23m is approximately 4.66%. §3.8: 'during the year some short-term borrowing was replaced with long-term PWLB borrowing at competitive rates of interest.' On the paper's own §8.11 rate table, 5-year maturity certainty at 31.3.2026 was 5.04% and 10-year 5.72% — EIP rates sit below Maturity rates because EIP amortises. We do not hold a historical EIP fixings series to reproduce each trade date exactly.

facts.value: Authority has decided NOT to use the 2026/27 MRP holiday provision. Legislation gives the option to reduce (or nil) the MRP charge for 2026/27 only; any MRP not made must be recovered over a maximum of 10 future years.

source.title: 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn Report — Appendix 1, Governance & Audit Committee, 4 June 2026

facts.note: Appendix §4.12, page 9. Rationale stated: 'In view of the overall balanced budget set for 2026/27, alongside the implication of higher MRP costs in subsequent years the Authority has decided not to use this provision.' Explicit opt-out is worth flagging — several councils in our library have taken up the holiday and rolled it forward.

summary.text:
Monmouthshire's 4 June 2026 report is a covering report plus a full Appendix 1 that carries every substantive table (Table 1 balance sheet, Table 3 borrowing, Table 4 new draws, Table 10 liability benchmark, Table 12 maturity structure). The covering report also reproduces the borrowing and non-treasury tables verbatim from the appendix — so the two documents are consistent throughout. The Section 151 role is referenced under Consultees as 'Deputy Chief Executive, Strategic Director Resources' but not named; the report author with a printed address is Daniel Francis, Finance Business Partner.

The PWLB loan-book reconciliation TIES. Paper Table 3 prints PWLB £158.7m at 3.7% weighted, 15.2 years weighted average maturity. Our file (108 PWLB loans at 31.3.2026) is £158,661,864 at 3.7247% — matches to the pound at the £158.66m level and to the decimal on rate. The balance sheet identity also ties: General Fund CFR £226.8m − External borrowing £197.6m − Other LT liabilities £1.8m = £27.4m against the paper's £27.5m internal borrowing (§2.2), £0.1m rounding on the intermediate Borrowing CFR line.

Three things stand out. First, Table 10 forecasts a £77.1m borrowing requirement by 31 March 2027 — one year out — driven almost entirely by the £70.1m fall in the current loan profile (£33m LA/Other short-term rolling off, plus PWLB and Welsh Gov short-dated maturities). Second, 30% of the book (£59.28m) sits inside 12 months at year end — mostly LA short-term but a scheduled refinancing lump. Third, the paper prints its own PWLB rate table at §8.11: the long end has since risen 0.11%-0.19% (10y 5.72% → 5.83%, 20y 6.23% → 6.38%, 50y 6.08% → 6.27% at 14 August 2026) and the 1-year is 0.09% lower. Monmouthshire holds no LOBOs (Table 3 shows nil at both dates), has opted out of the 2026/27 MRP holiday (§4.12), and took £23m of new long-dated PWLB in 2025/26 across four EIP tranches and one short Maturity at 4.51%-4.85% (Table 4).

officer.subject: Your Table 10's £77m, and where the long end sits since March
officer.body:
Hi Daniel,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the outturn report to your 4 June Governance & Audit Committee. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Appendix 1 is unusually complete for a covering-plus-appendix outturn — Table 10 in particular is one of the tighter liability-benchmark presentations we've read, with the current loan profile and forecast years alongside the benchmark itself.

The place to start is your PWLB position. Your Table 3 prints £158.7m at 3.7% weighted, 15.2 years average remaining maturity at 31 March 2026. Our file at the same date holds 108 PWLB loans totalling £158,661,864 at a weighted 3.7247% — ties to the pound at the £158.66m level and to the decimal on rate. Table 3's £5.9m Welsh Government interest-free loan and £33m of LA/Other short-term borrowing are outside our file (we hold PWLB only), but the PWLB slice reconciles.

The line that jumps off the page next is Table 10. Your liability benchmark projects a £77.1m borrowing requirement by 31 March 2027 — twelve months out — rising to £93.1m by 31 March 2029. The mechanics show through Table 12: 30% of your book (about £59m) sits inside 12 months at 31 March 2026, so most of the £77m is really the £70m fall in your current loan profile between now and next March — the £33m of short-term LA loans rolling off, plus the short-dated PWLB and Welsh Gov tranches, plus about £7m of rising benchmark. Not a hidden liability; a scheduled one. But the shape of the PWLB curve between now and next March determines the cost of a lot of debt in one window.

On which — a mark for §8.11 as at 31 March. Since then the PWLB 10-year certainty rate has moved from 5.72% to 5.83%, the 20-year from 6.23% to 6.38%, and the 50-year from 6.08% to 6.27% (PWLB notice 314/26 PM on 14 August 2026). The long end is roughly 0.11%-0.19% higher than the numbers your paper prints, and the 1-year is 0.09% lower at 4.95%. On the £16m of new EIP borrowing you disclose in Table 4 (four tranches at 4.51%-4.85% across five to ten years), the shape of today's curve helps frame what a replacement tranche might cost.

For where to look, pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity shows the whole sector's monthly PWLB draws by rate and maturity — useful for placing your own tranches against what other councils were paying that week. And pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis prices any council's PWLB book against the DMO's repayment curve daily. Indicative only — only the DMO can quote — and we don't model MRP or accounting treatment.

On training, three look relevant given your paper. The liability benchmark pathway, which is interactive and built on live data — worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes, and your Table 10 sits at the middle of that conversation. Refinancing risk, given the £77m falling due inside twelve months. And a session on EIP borrowing, since your Table 4 shows four EIP tranches taken in the year. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
